public_rationale: DeepMind's December 2021 Gopher report described scaling gains in reading comprehension and fact-checking, alongside little improvement on some logical-reasoning and common-sense tasks [e2]. The paper reported that the compared language models remained considerably below human performance on Winogrande, HellaSwag and PIQA [e1]. This supports the limited claim that gains coexisted with deficits on some measures [e1, e2]. In April 2022, Google reported that PaLM exceeded average human performance across a subset of 58 BIG-bench tasks and separately reported reasoning gains using scale with chain-of-thought prompting [e3]. Those results establish progress on other evaluations without eliminating the documented Gopher shortfalls [e1, e3].
limitations: The two supporting items describe the same Gopher research [e1, e2].
These benchmark results do not establish a universal inability to reason or a permanent limit on scaling [e1, e2].
PaLM's reported reasoning gains combine model scale with prompting changes; its above-average-human aggregate covers a broader task subset [e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Making large language models bigger helps in some ways, but on some reasoning and common-sense measures they still fall short.
conditions: on some measures of reasoning and common sense

statement.excerpt: Still further recent studies have reported that although making these immense models ever bigger helps in some respects, on some measures of reasoning and common sense, they continue to fall short.

from_speaker: making these immense models ever bigger helps in some respects
on some measures of reasoning and common sense
our_interpretation: This concerns results available when Marcus wrote, not whether later models overcame those limitations.
I interpret recent studies as work reported in 2021 and 2022 through the post date. The source does not specify an exact starting date.
The ordinary reading is that increasing model size improved some measured capabilities while leaving substantial deficits on some reasoning and common-sense tasks.
Falling short means documented weaknesses against relevant task or human-performance benchmarks. It does not require failure on every task or an absence of improvement.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary scaling research reports improvements on some tasks alongside substantial remaining weaknesses on particular reasoning and common-sense benchmarks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The relevant contemporary studies show that larger models eliminated the alleged reasoning and common-sense deficits, or that the reported combination of gains and remaining deficits was misrepresented. Success on other tasks alone does not contradict this limited claim.

evidence.locator: Section Gopher - A 280 billion parameter language model, second paragraph
evidence.explanation: The same paragraph reports gains in reading comprehension, fact-checking, and toxic-language identification before identifying reasoning and common-sense tasks with little scaling benefit. This directly matches the claim's combination of improvements and limitations, though it summarizes the same study as e1.

evidence.locator: Section Language Understanding and Generation, discussion of 58 BIG-bench tasks
evidence.explanation: PaLM exceeded average human performance across the reported BIG-bench subset; the announcement also reports reasoning gains from scale combined with chain-of-thought prompting. This qualifies any broader claim that reasoning cannot improve, but does not negate deficits on some measures.
